To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HES factors regulate dynamic transcriptional switching in the context of chromatin.
HES transcriptional repressing proteins dynamically repress genes by recruiting chromatin-modifying proteins and that this repression is required for maintaining multipotency.

(1) HES repressing transcription factors are involved in dynamic epigenetic regulation of gene expression; (2) HES factors are linked to the Polycomp-group of repressors, which are known to induce long-term chromatin changes; (3) HES factors also interact with other co-repressors that are not associated with long-term changes; (4) HES factors induce dynamic changes in chromatin, which are associated with cycling expression;

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HES family of transcription factors are key players in the dynamic control of chromatin structure and gene expression.
dynamic epigenetic regulation of transcription is a fundamental process, which is crucial in maintaining multipotent stem cells and their progenies.
HES proteins are important in the regulation of gene expression in a variety of developmental contexts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dynamic epigenetic regulation of gene expression is an important mechanism to control the timing and level of gene expression in development.
dynamic chromatin reprogramming is a key feature of the HES-mediated epigenetic control and that it can be used to generate a wide range of cell types from pluripotent stem cells.

dynamic epigenetic control of chromatin is an important aspect of the regulation of gene expression in development and that HES factors and associated chromatin modifiers are key players in this process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HES factors can act as dynamic palimpsests, which are capable of erasing and reprogramming chromatin states on their target genes.
HES repressing complexes can act as a paradigmatic example for dynamic chromatin reprogramming in development.
dynamic epigenetic changes are not just an interesting phenomenon, they are essential for the proper development of the organism and the maintenance of stem cells.
